findings.title: Malicious executable p.exe in staging directory c:\windows\temp\perfmon
findings.description: p.exe found at c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe, launched by cmd.exe (PID 5948) under a PowerShell C2 chain. YARA scan of the dumped binary confirmed Meterpreter named pipe transport string MSSE-7702-server at offset 0x4a9b9. The binary loaded full network and crypto stack including WININET, WS2_32, bcrypt, rsaenh.

evidence.raw_tool_output: 8260 p.exe 0x8c88af601580 2 - 0 False 2018-08-30 22:15:18.000000 UTC N/A; YARA MATCH: Meterpreter_NamedPipe_Transport at offset 0x4a9b9 (MSSE-) and 0x4a9c2 (-server)

findings.title: WmiPrvSE.exe spawned blank-cmdline powershell.exe (PID 8712) — WMI execution
findings.description: powershell.exe (PID 8712) was spawned by WmiPrvSE.exe (PID 2876) with a blank command line, indicating WMI-based remote code execution. This is the top of the attacker's execution chain. The process ran as spsql (Domain Admins) with High Mandatory Level.

evidence.raw_tool_output: 8712 2876 powershell.exe 0x8c88b47b9080 11 - 0 False 2018-08-30 16:43:36 UTC N/A; parent=WmiPrvSE.exe; SID includes S-1-5-21-...-512 (Domain Admins)

findings.title: 32-bit PowerShell stdin C2 shell (PID 5848) — attacker interactive session
findings.description: powershell.exe (PID 5848) running from SysWOW64 with '-Version 5.1 -s -NoLogo -NoProfile' was spawned by the WMI PowerShell. The -s flag routes I/O through stdin/stdout — the canonical PowerShell agent pattern used by frameworks such as PowerShell Empire. AMSI was loaded but likely bypassed in-memory. The process has been alive since 2018-08-30 16:43:42 UTC.

evidence.raw_tool_output: 5848 powershell.exe syswow64 -s flag; amsi.dll loaded at 0x70f30000; multiple unnamed DLLs present (reflective loading indicators)

findings.title: cmd.exe dropping and executing p.exe from staging path
findings.description: cmd.exe (PID 5948) was spawned by the PowerShell C2 shell (PID 5848) and executed 'c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe'. The staging path mimics a legitimate Windows directory (Perfmon) to blend in with legitimate activity.

findings.title: Nine short-lived rundll32.exe processes — shellcode injection launchers
findings.description: Nine rundll32.exe processes (PIDs 6768, 5452, 5588, 2216, 4108, 8148 from PS 5848; PIDs 5768, 7552, 1424 from p.exe) all had blank command lines and exited within 5–30 seconds. This pattern is consistent with reflective DLL/shellcode injection: spawn rundll32, inject shellcode via WriteProcessMemory, let it run, exit the host process.

evidence.raw_tool_output: PIDs 6768 5452 5588 2216 4108 8148 (PPID 5848) and 5768 7552 1424 (PPID 8260) — all null cmdlines, all exited within 30s of creation; date range 2018-08-30 18:31 to 2018-09-06 17:26

findings.title: C2 beaconing to internal host 172.16.4.10:8080 — multiple ESTABLISHED connections
findings.description: netscan shows 3 ESTABLISHED TCP connections from 172.16.6.11 to 172.16.4.10:8080, plus 7 CLOSE_WAIT and CLOSED connections to the same host/port. The volume of connections to port 8080 over multiple days (2018-08-30 to 2018-09-06) strongly indicates this is the C2 server. The ESTABLISHED connections have no PID annotation (process may have exited or connection belongs to an injected thread).

findings.title: Domain Admin spsql credentials used across entire attacker kill chain
findings.description: getsids confirmed that powershell.exe (8712), powershell.exe (5848), and p.exe (8260) all run as user spsql (S-1-5-21-...-1193) with Domain Admins (S-1-5-21-...-512), Administrators (S-1-5-32-544), and High Mandatory Level (S-1-16-12288). The attacker has complete domain-level control.

evidence.raw_tool_output: PID 8712,5848,8260 → spsql; S-1-5-32-544 (Administrators); S-1-5-21-...-512 (Domain Admins); S-1-16-12288 (High Mandatory Level)

findings.title: SMB lateral movement — ESTABLISHED connections to 172.16.4.5:445 and 172.16.7.15:445
findings.description: netscan shows two active SMB connections: 172.16.6.11:49763→172.16.4.5:445 (ESTABLISHED) and 172.16.6.11:59352→172.16.7.15:445 (ESTABLISHED). Additionally, incoming SMB from 172.16.6.14:65368 to 172.16.6.11:445 is ESTABLISHED. These connections indicate lateral movement and possible file staging via SMB with Domain Admin credentials.

findings.title: WinRM lateral movement attempt to 172.16.5.21:5985
findings.description: netscan records a CLOSED connection to 172.16.5.21:5985 (WinRM default port), indicating the attacker attempted or succeeded in moving laterally via PowerShell Remoting or WinRM. Also a CLOSED connection to 172.16.5.20:443. The rsydow-a user profile contains wsmprovhost.exe CLR logs, potentially indicating PS remoting activity under that account.

findings.title: External C2/download connections to 52.16.55.11:443 and 13.89.220.65:443
findings.description: netscan shows CLOSED connections to two external IPs: 52.16.55.11:443 (AWS EU-West-1 range) and 13.89.220.65:443 (Microsoft Azure). These may represent initial payload download, external C2 beaconing, or data exfiltration. Both are HTTPS connections.

findings.title: LDAP query to 172.16.4.4:389 — Active Directory reconnaissance
findings.description: A CLOSED TCP connection to 172.16.4.4:389 (LDAP) indicates Active Directory enumeration. With Domain Admin credentials, the attacker can query all AD objects, enumerate users, computers, and GPOs.

findings.title: No registry-based persistence installed — negative finding
findings.description: registry.printkey on SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and RunOnce showed no attacker-controlled entries for the spsql account. svcscan revealed no services with paths in user-writable locations. The attacker achieved persistent access through the long-lived powershell.exe C2 shell (since 2018-08-30 16:43) rather than registry persistence.

evidence.raw_tool_output: spsql ntuser.dat Run key: empty (no values); spsql RunOnce key: empty; svcscan: no services with paths in temp/appdata/users

findings.title: OUTLOOK.EXE (PID 8128) malfind RWX regions — initial injection suspicion
findings.description: malfind flagged two RWX VadS regions in OUTLOOK.EXE (PID 8128) starting with byte pattern 64 74 72 52 (dtrR). These regions were initially considered for injection.

findings.title: UpdaterUI.exe (PID 6036) malfind RWX region — null bytes
findings.description: malfind flagged a 1-page RWX VadS region in UpdaterUI.exe (PID 6036, McAfee Agent) filled with null bytes interspersed with address-pattern bytes.

findings.title: powershell.exe (PID 8712) malfind RWX regions — initial injection suspicion
findings.description: malfind flagged three RWX VadS regions in powershell.exe (PID 8712) containing the byte pattern ee ff ee ff. These were initially considered suspicious.

evidence.raw_tool_output: 8712 powershell.exe 0x1b4ce1a0000 PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE 8 pages; hex: ee ff ee ff 02 00 00 00... (CLR heap marker pattern)
